Solve a Linear-Quadratic System Using Substitution
How can you use substitution to solve this system? (y=3x^2+3x-5), (2x-y=3)
The first equation provides an expression for y in terms of x. Substitute this expression in the second equation.
(2x-(3x^2+3x-5)=3)
(2x-3x^2-3x+5=3)
(3x^2+x-2=0)
((x+1)(3x-2)=0)
So (x=-1) and (x=(2)/(3)) are solutions of this quadratic equation.
When (x=-1), (y=2(-1)-3), or -5. When (x=(2)/(3)), (y=2((2)/(3))-3), or (-(5)/(3)).
The solutions of the system are (-1,-5) and ((2)/(3),-(5)/(3)).
